title: THE BLAME PIE
goal: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
steps:
1. Imagine A Pie — Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation.
2. Share The Slices — In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
3. Check The Whole — Make sure all slices together equal 100.
4. Find Your Slice — Focus only on your true share.
5. Choose Repair — Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility.
win: ✓ My slice stayed mine; the rest went back to the whole pie.
supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Repair”; release extra blame.
• Pulled back? Touch “Check The Whole”.
• “Find Your Slice” keeps blame in proportion.
• Compare “Imagine A Pie” with “Choose Repair”.
• I can use “Share The Slices” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Imagine A Pie → Share The Slices → Check The Whole → Find Your Slice → Choose Repair
safety:
PAUSE
Set it down if sharing turns into punishment or erases genuine accountability.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE LIFE DIRECTION TEST
goal: A thought can sound true and still drive badly.
steps:
1. Picture — Picture two arrows.
2. Make Room — One shows the next hour if you obey the thought; the other reveals what unfolds over sixty minutes when you make room for it but follow a chosen value.
3. Name Likely — Name the likely behaviour at each arrow’s end.
4. Select Direction — Select by direction, not by mental volume.
win: ✓ The room became larger than the mental pull.
supports:
• Exhale after “Select Direction”; keep the compass.
• Loop back? Use “Name Likely”.
• “Name Likely” keeps meaning in motion.
• Compare “Picture” with “Select Direction”.
• I can use “Make Room” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Picture → Make Room → Name Likely → Select Direction

GOAL
A thought can sound true and still drive badly.

1. Picture — Picture two arrows.

3. Name Likely — Name the likely behaviour at each arrow’s end.
4. Select Direction — Select by direction, not by mental volume.

title: MORE THAN THIS STATE
goal: A single moment cannot legally seize your whole identity.
steps:
1. Carry Qualities — Name three roles you carry, two qualities others have witnessed, and one state present today.
2. Imagine Large — Imagine a large Focus on around all six.
3. Place Painful — Place the current painful content inside, not across, the boundary.
4. Ask Part — Ask which part of the larger system should lead the one simple action.
win: ✓ This state stayed one part of me, not the whole system.
supports:
• Exhale after “Ask Part”; release extra load.
• Shortcut: “Place Painful”, once.
• “Place Painful” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• What changed: “Carry Qualities” → “Ask Part”?
• I can use “Imagine Large” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Carry Qualities → Imagine Large → Place Painful → Ask Part

TITLE
MORE THAN THIS STATE

GOAL
A single moment cannot legally seize your whole identity.

RITUAL
1. Carry Qualities — Name three roles you carry, two qualities others have witnessed, and one state present today.
2. Imagine Large — Imagine a large Focus on around all six.
3. Place Painful — Place the current painful content inside, not across, the boundary.
4. Ask Part — Ask which part of the larger system should lead the one simple action.

WIN
✓ This state stayed one part of me, not the whole system.

• Exhale after “Ask Part”; release extra load.
• Shortcut: “Place Painful”, once.
• “Place Painful” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• What changed: “Carry Qualities” → “Ask Part”?
• I can use “Imagine Large” without carrying it all.

FORMULA FLOW
Carry Qualities → Imagine Large → Place Painful → Ask Part

PAUSE
Use simple grounding instead if expansion feels abstract or dissociative.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHAT JOB IS THIS FEELING DOING?
goal: An emotion is a messenger with several departments.
steps:
1. Ask Separately — Ask three questions separately: What change is it signalling?
2. Prepare Action — What action is it preparing?
3. Communicating — What is it communicating to others?
4. Keep Concrete — Keep answers concrete.
5. Use the Message — Use the information. Keep the behaviour under your supervision.
win: ✓ The feeling delivered its message without taking over behaviour.
supports:
• Exhale after “Use the Message”; let feeling settle.
• Pulled back? Touch “Communicating”.
• “Keep Concrete” separates feeling from fact.
• “Ask Separately” to “Use the Message”: what loosened?
• I can use “Prepare Action” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Ask Separately → Prepare Action → Communicating → Keep Concrete → Use the Message

5. Place Attention — End by selecting where attention belongs now.

TITLE
FINISH THE LOOK

GOAL
Defence narrows the world; orientation in the present reopens it.

RITUAL
1. Let Eyes — Let your eyes move before your head.
2. Scan Left — Slowly scan left, centre, right, behind if safe, and toward an exit.
3. Name Cues — Name present cues of choice, support, and distance from threat.
4. Allow Neck — Allow the neck to follow only within comfort.
5. Place Attention — End by selecting where attention belongs now.

WIN
✓ Now is back in the foreground.

• Gently exhale after “Place Attention”; no forcing.
• If it flares, choose “Name Cues”.
• “Allow Neck” keeps sensation as data.
• Before/after: “Let Eyes” → “Place Attention”.
• I can use “Scan Left” while sensation stays.

title: TRACK WHAT HOLDS
goal: Support becomes stronger when it receives precise attention.
steps:
1. Locate Bodily — Locate one bodily sign of steadiness—warmth, pressure, uprightness, ease, or a capable impulse.
2. Describe Boundaries — Say its boundaries and changes for twenty seconds.
3. Ask Memory — Ask what memory, person, posture, or environment strengthens it by one degree.
4. Add Ingredient — Add only that ingredient.
win: ✓ One useful ingredient found; the rest can stay off the recipe.
supports:
• Exhale after “Add Ingredient”; let wanting crest.
• Skip replay; use “Ask Memory”.
• “Ask Memory” keeps wanting off controls.
• “Locate Bodily” to “Add Ingredient”: what loosened?
• I can use “Describe Boundaries” without obeying the urge.

title: LET BREATH BREATHE YOU
goal: Remove the manager from respiration.
steps:
1. Follow Breaths — Follow three natural breaths exactly as they occur.
2. Leave Breath Alone — Do not deepen, slow, count, or improve them.
3. Start — Notice where each begins by itself and where it ends without instruction.
4. Let Body — Between breaths, let the body choose again.
5. Witness Motion — Your only action is witnessing what already knows how to move.
win: ✓ The thought moved from identity to object.
supports:
• Exhale after “Witness Motion”; watch the thought.
• Pulled back? Touch “Start”.
• “Let Body” proves thought is observable.
• Before/after: “Follow Breaths” → “Witness Motion”.
• I can use “Leave Breath Alone” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Follow Breaths → Leave Breath Alone → Start → Let Body → Witness Motion

title: THE EVEN BRIDGE
goal: Symmetry gives attention a simple crossing.
steps:
1. Pick Requires — Pick a count that requires no effort.
2. Count Exhale — Inhale for that count, exhale for the same count, and leave any natural pause untouched.
3. Imagine Pair — Imagine each pair forming equal sides of a bridge.
4. Complete Few — Complete a few balanced crossings, then let counting dissolve.
win: ✓ Noise separated into something the mind can hold.
supports:
• Exhale after “Complete Few”; then keep moving.
• Skip replay; use “Imagine Pair”.
• “Imagine Pair” proves motion is available.
• Difference check: “Pick Requires” → “Complete Few”.
• I can use “Count Exhale” before motivation.
formula_flow: Pick Requires → Count Exhale → Imagine Pair → Complete Few

title: WHAT SURVIVES THREE STATES?
goal: Compare experience across waking, dreaming, and dreamless sleep.
steps:
1. Picture Appears — Picture what appears in waking, what appears in dreams, and what is absent or inferred in deep sleep.
2. Ask Claims — Ask which claims of identity remain supported across all three.
3. Hold Conclusions — Hold conclusions lightly; this is an inquiry into ongoing sense, not a demand for belief.
win: ✓ The social scoreboard stopped being the whole room.
supports:
• Exhale after “Hold Conclusions”; drop the scoreboard.
• Skip replay; use “Ask Claims”.
• “Ask Claims” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• Difference check: “Picture Appears” → “Hold Conclusions”.
• I can use “Ask Claims” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Picture Appears → Ask Claims → Hold Conclusions
safety:
PAUSE
Discontinue if sleep-related inquiry worsens insomnia or unreality.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SAME VALUE, TWO OUTCOMES
goal: Stability is trained before the verdict arrives.
steps:
1. Imagine Action — Imagine the action succeeding.
2. State Governing — State what that value asks of you next.
3. Imagine Failing — Imagine it failing.
4. State Value — State how the same value responds there.
5. Let Outcome — Let outcome alter strategy, not your ethical centre.
win: ✓ Meaning found a next move without denying the pain.
supports:
• Exhale after “Let Outcome”; keep both sides.
• Pulled back? Touch “Imagine Failing”.
• “State Value” widens the evidence field.
• Keep one lesson: “Imagine Action” → “Let Outcome”.
• I can use “State Governing” before concluding.
formula_flow: Imagine Action → State Governing → Imagine Failing → State Value → Let Outcome
safety:
PAUSE

title: EMPTY THE MENTAL COUNTERTOP
goal: Short-term attention is not permanent storage.
steps:
1. Question Promise — Catch every task, question, promise, and loose obligation into one trusted place.
2. Empty First — Do not organise while emptying.
3. Sort Entries — When the mind offers silence, sort entries into do, schedule, delegate, reference, or delete.
4. Choose Physical — Choose only the first physical action.
win: ✓ Mental countertop cleared. One physical move remains.
supports:
• One exhale after “Choose Physical”; redirect attention.
• On return: “Sort Entries”.
• “Sort Entries” proves one signal leads.
• “Choose Physical”: what changed from “Question Promise”?
• I can use “Empty First” amid noise.

title: IMPACT IS KNOWN; MOTIVE IS PENDING
goal: Do not let mind-reading erase visible harm.
steps:
1. Separate Unknown — Picture three separate statements: their behaviour; what effect it had; what you do not know about intention.
2. Base — Base your next boundary on behaviour and impact.
3. Leave Motive — Leave motive open until reliable evidence or direct communication updates it.
win: ✓ The need to know shrank below the need to live the next minute.
supports:
• Exhale after “Leave Motive”; leave it unanswered.
• Use “Base” on return.
• “Base” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• “Separate Unknown” versus “Leave Motive”: what eased?
• I can use “Base” without a guarantee.

title: BRAID THE SIGNALS
goal: Two competing experiences can become one pattern.
steps:
1. Choose Signals — Choose the two signals fighting for attention.
2. Alternate B — Alternate A–B–A–B at a slow fixed rhythm.
3. Hold Time — Then hold both at the same time for one interval, noticing difference without choosing.
4. Decide After — Decide only after the braid is complete.
win: ✓ Two competing signals became one braid I could actually read.
supports:
• One exhale after “Decide After”; redirect attention.
• Return once to “Hold Time”.
• “Hold Time” proves one signal leads.
• Compare “Choose Signals” with “Decide After”.
• I can use “Alternate B” amid noise.

title: MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT
goal: Equal pressure gives restless energy a shared route down.
steps:
1. Press Equal — Press palms together—or both hands into one cushion—at about twenty percent effort. Keep breathing ordinary.
2. Match Force — Adjust until neither side wins and the pressure feels equal. Hold that match for two seconds.
3. Step Down — Lower both sides together through three gentle levels: fifteen, ten, then five percent.
4. Reach Zero — Reach zero, rest both hands on a stable surface, and observe whether the urge to press returns.
win: ✓ I matched the pressure, brought it back to zero, and checked what remained.
supports:

• If it flares, choose “Step Down”.
• “Step Down” proves choice interrupted habit.
• What lost power: “Press Equal” → “Reach Zero”?
• I can use “Match Force” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Press Equal → Match Force → Step Down → Reach Zero

title: ASK THE QUESTION FEAR KEEPS ANSWERING
goal: Direct data can update the relationship model.
steps:
1. Picture Assumption — Picture the assumption driving your reaction.
2. Question Whose — Convert it into one clear, non-leading question whose answer could prove the assumption wrong.
3. Ask Suitable — Ask at a suitable time, listen fully, and compare reply plus later behaviour with the original model.
win: ✓ Fear finally answered the question it had been answering for me.
supports:
• Exhale after “Ask Suitable”; soften the jaw.
• Shortcut: “Question Whose”, once.
• “Question Whose” keeps clarity above heat.
• “Picture Assumption” to “Ask Suitable”: what loosened?
• I can use “Question Whose” without extra heat.

steps:

• “Use Line” proves choice interrupted habit.
• What changed: “Question Task” → “Imagine Boundary”?
• I can use “Use Line” before autopilot.

title: MARK THE QUALITY DROP
goal: Analysis needs an exit before fatigue corrupts it.
steps:
1. Repeat No — Define your personal decline signs in advance: rereading, harsher certainty, slower comprehension, repeated searches, no new distinctions.
2. Stop Last — When two appear, stop and hold the last reliable conclusion.
3. Start Recovery — Recovery precedes any reopening.
win: ✓ I caught the moment thinking quality dropped and exited before fatigue took over.
supports:

• On return: “Stop Last”.
• “Stop Last” widens the evidence field.
• “Start Recovery”: what changed from “Repeat No”?
• I can use “Stop Last” before concluding.

TITLE

GOAL
Analysis needs an exit before fatigue corrupts it.

RITUAL
1. Repeat No — Define your personal decline signs in advance: rereading, harsher certainty, slower comprehension, repeated searches, no new distinctions.

3. Start Recovery — Recovery precedes any reopening.

WIN
✓ I caught the moment thinking quality dropped and exited before fatigue took over.

• Exhale after “Start Recovery”; keep both sides.
• On return: “Stop Last”.
• “Stop Last” widens the evidence field.
• “Start Recovery”: what changed from “Repeat No”?
• I can use “Stop Last” before concluding.

FORMULA FLOW
Repeat No → Stop Last → Start Recovery

PAUSE
Continue only when delay creates greater risk than reduced quality.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: REPLAY THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
goal: Find the turning point, not another theory about the whole conversation.
steps:
1. Recall Exchange — Choose no more than ten seconds of the interaction, beginning before the moment that felt different.
2. Halve Speed — Replay it once in imagination at half speed. Keep only what you can actually observe: words, pauses, volume, face, and movement.
3. Shift — Stop at the first change and name it without motive: ‘the pause lengthened,’ ‘the volume rose,’ or ‘the reply shortened.’
4. Keep Fact — Keep that one fact. End the replay before building another explanation.
win: ✓ The worry cycle lost its automatic restart.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Keep Fact”; orient to now.
• Use “Shift” on return.
• “Shift” moves memory toward then.
• What lost power: “Recall Exchange” → “Keep Fact”?
• I can use “Halve Speed” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Recall Exchange → Halve Speed → Shift → Keep Fact
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if replay raises distress, becomes compulsive, or concerns abuse or danger that requires support and protection.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS
goal: A five-tile loop is much easier to catch.
steps:
1. No Sentences — Imagine five boxes. Do not use full sentences.
2. Imagine Five Signs — Give each of the last five thought turns one simple inner picture.
3. Spot The Return — Notice the first picture whose meaning comes back later.
4. Choose An Exit — At the next box, picture one real fact to check or one small action to take, then stop imagining.
win: ✓ Five icons exposed the repeat—and one place to exit.
supports:
• Exhale after “Choose An Exit”; end the lap.
• If it flares, choose “Spot The Return”.
• “Spot The Return” proves loops can stop.
• Look back: “No Sentences” → “Choose An Exit”.
• I can use “Imagine Five Signs” without another lap.
formula_flow: No Sentences → Imagine Five Signs → Spot The Return → Choose An Exit
safety:
PAUSE
Do not imagine this while driving; stop if the mental sequence becomes compulsive, perfectionistic, or more distressing than the thought.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

RITUAL
1. No Sentences — Imagine five boxes. Do not use full sentences.
2. Imagine Five Signs — Give each of the last five thought turns one simple inner picture.
3. Spot The Return — Notice the first picture whose meaning comes back later.
4. Choose An Exit — At the next box, picture one real fact to check or one small action to take, then stop imagining.

WIN
✓ Five icons exposed the repeat—and one place to exit.

• Exhale after “Choose An Exit”; end the lap.
• If it flares, choose “Spot The Return”.
• “Spot The Return” proves loops can stop.
• Look back: “No Sentences” → “Choose An Exit”.
• I can use “Imagine Five Signs” without another lap.

FORMULA FLOW
No Sentences → Imagine Five Signs → Spot The Return → Choose An Exit

PAUSE
Do not imagine this while driving; stop if the mental sequence becomes compulsive, perfectionistic, or more distressing than the thought.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SCULPT THE PROBLEM
goal: Abstract distress changes when relationships become physical.
steps:
1. Use Small — Represent the problem using small objects for people, obstacles, resources, and goals.
2. Feel Arrange — Arrange them as they feel now.
3. Move Object — Move only one object or distance to create a more workable configuration.
4. Name Real — Name the real-life action equivalent to that move.
win: ✓ The abstract problem moved on the table—and revealed a real-world move.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Name Real”; orient to now.
• Loop back? Use “Move Object”.
• “Move Object” moves memory toward then.
• Look back: “Use Small” → “Name Real”.
• I can use “Feel Arrange” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Use Small → Feel Arrange → Move Object → Name Real

title: REMEMBER THE FUTURE IN ADVANCE
goal: The future gets easier when it already feels familiar.
steps:
1. Create Memory — Create a memory-like scene set just after completing the action.
2. Include Time — Include time, location, body posture, one sensory cue, along with what you did when difficulty appeared.
3. Look Backward — Look backward from that imagined completion to the first real movement and do it now.
win: ✓ The future felt remembered enough for the first movement to become obvious.
supports:
• One exhale after “Look Backward”; redirect attention.
• Catch restart with “Include Time”.
• “Include Time” proves one signal leads.
• At “Look Backward”, compare “Create Memory”.
• I can use “Include Time” amid noise.
formula_flow: Create Memory → Include Time → Look Backward
safety:
PAUSE
Keep future scenes realistic rather than using fantasy as avoidance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: INTERVIEW THE OBSTACLE
goal: Resistance may be protecting something your plan ignored.
steps:
1. Give Obstacle — Give the obstacle a character and ask three questions: What are you protecting?
2. Ask Fear — What do you fear will happen?
3. Make Step — What would make one step acceptable?
4. Picture Negotiate — Picture its answers, then negotiate a small action that protects the valid need without handing over total control.
win: ✓ Resistance revealed the need it was trying to protect.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Picture Negotiate”; orient to now.
• Loop back? Use “Make Step”.
• “Make Step” moves memory toward then.
• “Give Obstacle” versus “Picture Negotiate”: what eased?
• I can use “Ask Fear” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Give Obstacle → Ask Fear → Make Step → Picture Negotiate
safety:
PAUSE
Do not personify intrusive voices or experiences if that worsens symptoms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: IMAGINE THE INNER MACHINE
goal: Chaos becomes editable after signals and loops are visible.
steps:
1. Imagine The Parts — Imagine the trigger, meaning, physical feeling, urge, action, result, and feedback.
2. See The Links — Imagine how each part affects the next and where the loop returns.
3. Find the Lever — Notice one place where a small change may shift the whole loop.
4. Test It — Try that small change once.
win: ✓ One inner-machine dial moved; chaos became editable.
supports:
• Exhale after “Test It”; mark the pause.
• Skip replay; use “Find the Lever”.
• “Find the Lever” proves choice interrupted habit.
• “Imagine The Parts” versus “Test It”: what eased?
• I can use “See The Links” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Imagine The Parts → See The Links → Find the Lever → Test It
safety:
PAUSE
Keep the mental picture simple. Stop if you begin analysing without taking action.

steps:

• I can use “Give Posture” while fear stays loud.

title: WHAT WOULD THIS FACT CHANGE?
goal: Missing information must earn its collection cost.
steps:
1. Point Positive — For every desired data point, picture how a positive, negative, or neutral result would alter the decision.
2. Stop Collecting — If no result changes action, stop collecting it.
3. Test Relevance — Prioritise the fact with the largest possible decision swing.
win: ✓ Asked what the missing fact could actually change before paying to collect it.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Test Relevance”; orient to now.
• Loop back? Use “Stop Collecting”.
• “Stop Collecting” moves memory toward then.
• Keep one lesson: “Point Positive” → “Test Relevance”.
• I can use “Stop Collecting” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Point Positive → Stop Collecting → Test Relevance

goal: Sunk cost is history, not future value.

title: GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE
goal: A rule may fit one situation without ruling your whole life.
steps:
1. Name The Belief — Say the belief silently.
2. Imagine Four Limits — Think about when, where, with whom, and under what conditions it may be true.
3. Test Inside — Picture one real case where it fits.
4. Test Outside — Picture one real case where it does not fit.
5. Shrink the Rule — Say a smaller, more accurate version of the belief.
win: ✓ The belief got a postcode instead of a passport to everywhere.
supports:
• Exhale after “Shrink the Rule”; release extra blame.
• Catch restart with “Test Inside”.
• “Test Outside” keeps blame in proportion.
• What changed: “Name The Belief” → “Shrink the Rule”?
• I can use “Imagine Four Limits” without owning everything.

content:
TITLE
GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE

GOAL
A rule may fit one situation without ruling your whole life.

RITUAL
1. Name The Belief — Say the belief silently.
2. Imagine Four Limits — Think about when, where, with whom, and under what conditions it may be true.
3. Test Inside — Picture one real case where it fits.
4. Test Outside — Picture one real case where it does not fit.
5. Shrink the Rule — Say a smaller, more accurate version of the belief.

WIN
✓ The belief got a postcode instead of a passport to everywhere.

• Exhale after “Shrink the Rule”; release extra blame.
• Catch restart with “Test Inside”.
• “Test Outside” keeps blame in proportion.
• What changed: “Name The Belief” → “Shrink the Rule”?
• I can use “Imagine Four Limits” without owning everything.

FORMULA FLOW
Name The Belief → Imagine Four Limits → Test Inside → Test Outside → Shrink the Rule

PAUSE
Do not use belief boundaries to minimise abuse, discrimination, medical facts, legal duties, or immediate danger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
